item.title: The Erosion of Trust and Empathy
item.lead: In the dossier, trust is the central societal infrastructure which, according to the hypothesis, comes under pressure when interaction is increasingly monetized or scripted.

blocks.text: The source describes a dichotomy between unconditional attention and priced attention. In one situation, the other person is a human who responds because they want to; in the other situation, the contact is part of a service with a rate, limit, or paywall. When an individual is confronted with the second form multiple times, it can influence their expectations regarding the first form.

Distrust is added to this. The dossier states that the user does not always know whether they are dealing with a unique person, a team, or a bot. The creator side, in turn, can learn that the other party should primarily be viewed as a paying user or a risk profile. This creates a mutual suspicion which, according to the source, can permeate the physical world.

The analysis is psychological in nature, but not the same as a proven effect. To test the hypothesis, one would, for example, need longitudinal studies, interviews, and controlled comparisons. The source primarily provides an explanatory model.

The practical significance, however, remains clear: trust is difficult to scale. Precisely for this reason, an economic system that attempts to standardize human proximity can produce tension between efficiency and authenticity.
